# MT-05. Who signs in, and what an idle home writes

## Goal

A person who signs in to an operator's server can be reached at an address their provider vouches for, the operator's own pages are named as the server's own when they ask a person to sign in, and an idle server writes nothing a backup replicator has to ship.

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- an operator's own clients named as the server's own on the consent page (`RemoteServerConfig.operatorClients`, each a Client ID Metadata Document client with the name the operator gives it), with consent still asked once per account and never skipped;
- GitHub sign-in naming the person's verified primary address: the adapter asks for `user:email` and fills `SignInIdentity.email` from `GET /user/emails` with `emailVerified: true`, and gives no verified address when GitHub has none;
- an open hosted home's high-water marks (`home_cursor`) written only when they change, not every 10 s while nothing happens, so an idle server makes no writes a backup replicator has to ship.

Design detail for this package:

- A maintenance unit (D152): it owns no requirement. Its scope is the three items below, each closed with its check through the real interface (a real `mostra-runtime server` with its fake GitHub, a metadata-document client and real owner instances, as WP-30's sign-in suites run them) and a seeded violation red on the old code; the checks it adds extend MC-04's (the consent page), HY-08's (sign-in's identity) and RM-03's (the self-hosted server and its backups) rows. Every change is additive within `OPERATOR_REVISION` `2026-11-08` and the configuration's keys, so it ships in a minor release.
- **An operator's own clients on the consent page** (#168). Today the consent page names every Client ID Metadata Document client unverified, so an operator's own page that signs people in through the server reads like a stranger's app. Add `RemoteServerConfig.operatorClients: [{ clientId, name }]`, each a metadata-document client ID the operator vouches for: the consent page names such a client by the name the operator gives it, as the server's own, with no "unverified"; its redirect URIs still come from its document; consent is still asked once per account and client, never skipped. Any other metadata-document client is unchanged, and an entry the server can't use stops it with `MOSTRA_REMOTE_CONFIG_INVALID` naming the key.
- **GitHub's verified address** (#171). Today the GitHub adapter asks for no scope and reads `GET /user`, which gives an address only when the person made one public. Ask for `user:email` (read-only access to the account's addresses) and fill `SignInIdentity.email` with the primary address GitHub marks verified, from `GET /user/emails`, with `emailVerified: true`; with no such address it gives none. A person can grant less than the adapter asks on GitHub's screen, and GitHub's answer can fail: neither fails the sign-in.
- **What an idle home writes** (#186). Today an open hosted home's `home_cursor` row (DATA_MODEL §7.1) is written every 10 s whether or not a mark moved, so a server with one linked owner and nothing happening commits a transaction to its directory every 10 s, which a WAL replicator ships to its replica. Write it while the home is open only when its incarnation, `high_cursor` or `relay_high` differs from the row; the writes at opening and closing stay. The restore rule reads the marks, never `updated_at`, so restores rotate the incarnation as FAILURE_MODEL §11.2 says.
- Add MT-05's own decision entry, the dossier text each item changes (INTERFACES §18.1, §18.5; DATA_MODEL §7.1), the self-hosting page (what `user:email` asks of a person, and `operatorClients`), the runtime's `AGENTS.md` and a changeset whose release notes name the change people see on GitHub's own consent screen.

## Out of scope

- The hosted page's performance report (#167, WP-20's).
- Homes an organization owns (WP-33 to WP-35).

## Acceptance evidence

each change's check through the real interface (a real `mostra-runtime server` with its fake GitHub, a metadata-document client and real owner instances, as WP-30's sign-in suites run them), with a seeded violation red on the old code; the self-hosting page says what `user:email` asks of a person and what `operatorClients` does; the release notes name the change to GitHub's own consent screen.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- People who signed in with GitHub before see GitHub's consent screen once more, for the new scope: the release notes say so.
- The marks are the witness of a restore together with the owner instance (FAILURE_MODEL §11.2): a tick that skips a write must skip only when the row already holds what the home reached.

## Handoff

An operator's own sign-in page reads as the server's own, a GitHub sign-in names the person's verified address, and an idle server is quiet. The operating layer's next package raises its pins and takes the three requests' issues.
